subject: Energy
title: Clean Cooking Challenge
description: A 60-second lesson on Clean Cooking Challenge.

hook.text: 2.3 billion people cook on open fires or crude stoves—burning wood, charcoal, or animal dung inside their homes.

buildup.text: Smoke from cooking fires contains fine particles and carbon monoxide—causing lung disease, heart disease, and cancer.

discovery.text: Improved cookstoves cut fuel use and smoke by 50–90%—simple design changes like insulation and chimneys save lives.

twist.text: LPG gas and electric stoves exist but aren't affordable or available in many places—the last mile is the hardest.

climax.text: Clean cooking remains the most underfunded energy access issue—affecting mostly women who spend hours gathering fuel.

punchline.text: 3 million deaths a year from cooking smoke—a solvable tragedy.

quiz.question: How many people cook with polluting fuels globally?
